blind_target.outcome_quote:
This model
has previously been motivated based on data showing
that organized (and thus predictable) percepts lead to
reduced activation levels on the primary visual cortex
(Fang et al., 2008; Murray et al., 2002). The results of
the current study replicate this reduction, but ﬁnd that
this reduction is not speciﬁc to the sensory representation of this stimulus; rather, it also occurs in retinotopic
regions that do not respond to the sensory onset of the
stimulus. Importantly however this reduction is not
found in all visual areas (which might suggest a general

blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The V1 decrease and LO increase replicate, but the paper expressly contrasts its retinotopically nonspecific decrease with Fang et al.’s claim of retinotopic specificity. Confirming the decrease alone is an effect-specific comparison, not a verdict on the replication as a whole. Indeed this assumption was made explicit in Fang et al. (2008), who stated that ‘‘we are conﬁdent that the modulations in the fMRI signal that we observed occurred in the retinotopic representation of the stimulus and not in immediately adjacent retinotopic regions’’ (p. 6). In contrast, when we investigated this directly it became evident that, although there was a clear reduction in activation at the retinotopic location of the stimuli, this reduction did not appear to be speciﬁc to, or even selectively stronger in, the retinotopic location of the stimulus.

blind_target.evidence_quote: A pilot RCT with 156 youth found positive impacts on multi-informant (child, caregiver, teacher) reports of mental health functioning (including trauma symptoms), mental health services, and quality of life ( Taussig & Culhane, 2010 ). The current study sought to replicate and extend the mental health findings of the pilot FHF trial by adding data from five additional cohorts ( N =270) as well as examine moderating effects.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Intervention youth scored significantly lower on the mental health index ( β = −.11; t = −2.32; p < .05), posttraumatic stress symptoms ( β = −.09; t = −2.01; p < .05) and dissociation scales ( β = −.12; t = −2.76; p < .01), and they were less likely to be receiving mental health treatment at T2 (B = −.47; Wald = 4.43; p =.04). Intervention and control groups did not differ on quality of life or psychotropic medication use.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The original pilot showed improvements in mental health, services and quality of life. This study confirms the first two but finds no quality-of-life difference. Discussion confirms particular benefits, without an overall replication verdict covering all outcomes.
blind_target.title: Impact of a mentoring and skills group program on mental health outcomes for maltreated children in foster care.

blind_target.evidence_quote: In the FHF pilot study we found that (1) severity of neglect did not moderate outcomes, suggesting that children with severe neglect histories were just as likely to benefit from the intervention as those with less severe neglect histories ( Taussig, Culhane, Garrido, Knudtson, & Petrenko, 2013 ) but that (2) level of risk (i.e., exposure to ACEs) did moderate some outcomes (i.e., posttraumatic stress and dissociative symptoms), such that maltreated children exposed to a relatively higher number of ACEs did not experience the same reduction in trauma symptoms as children exposed to fewer adversities ( Weiler & Taussig, 2017 ). There were no a priori hypotheses about the direction of the potential moderating effects with the exception of the ACEs measure; based on our prior research, we hypothesized that those children with fewer ACEs would demonstrate greater program effects on trauma symptomatology.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Forty-two analyses were conducted and three interaction terms were statistically significant. The baseline ACEs measure significantly moderated the intervention’s impact on T2 youth-reported posttraumatic stress symptoms ( β = .15; t = 2.23; p < .05) and quality of life ( β = −.15; t = −2.06; p < .05).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The original risk moderation affected posttraumatic stress and dissociation; only posttraumatic stress moderation recurs among those two. Quality-of-life moderation is additional. Discussion confirms the fewer-ACEs pattern on some outcomes, rather than an overall verdict covering both original trauma outcomes. The new cohorts are pooled with the pilot sample, so the test is only partly independent.
